headline: Jordy and Ben Go 2-0, Pool Lead Stretches to Three Games
dek: Three head-to-heads delivered decisive swings while the top two entrants pulled further away from the field. Week 12's Thanksgiving slate brings four more pool collisions.
takeaways: Only two 2-0 weeks in a slate featuring three head-to-heads — Jordy and Ben now sit comfortably ahead of the chasing pack.
All three head-to-heads went the favourite's way: Jordy over Adrian, Matej over Bill, Taras over Orest in the week's wildest finish.
Ben's Niners and Texans combined to outscore their opponents 61-13, the most lopsided double-win of the season.
The middle of the standings remains a logjam — only four points separate Chris in second from Orest in seventh.

games.text:
Ben's Texans dismantled the Colts in the kind of complete performance Houston desperately needed to keep any playoff hopes alive. C.J. Stroud was surgical — 21-of-27 for 194 yards and three touchdowns — while David Montgomery churned out 107 yards on 26 carries to control the clock. Indianapolis managed just 144 passing yards and 21 rushing yards from Jonathan Taylor, never threatening after the opening quarter.

The blowout gives Ben a crucial 23-point boost in his weeklong rampage and lifts Houston to 4-6, still three games back of the final wild card spot but at least mathematically alive. The Texans face a massive head-to-head next Sunday when Orest's Ravens come to town — a loss there could effectively end Houston's season, while a win would pull Ben within a game of Orest in the standings.

Chris's Bills did what good teams do to bad ones, dispatching Miami with a workmanlike 26-9 victory that keeps Buffalo atop the AFC at 9-1. Josh Allen threw for 304 yards but was uncharacteristically careless with two interceptions, while James Cook III did the heavy lifting on the ground with 89 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries. The Dolphins managed just 102 passing yards from Kolby McCord and never found any rhythm.

The win keeps Chris one game clear of Jordy for the pool lead, though that margin could evaporate quickly — Chris faces two massive head-to-heads in Week 12, starting with Tymko's Chiefs on Thanksgiving night. Buffalo's remaining schedule is brutal, and the Bills will need to be sharper than they were against Miami if they want to hold serve.

Bill's Cowboys put on an offensive clinic in Arlington, with Dak Prescott going 28-of-33 for 325 yards and four touchdowns in a 51-30 shellacking of Tennessee. CeeDee Lamb caught 11 passes for 132 yards and a score, while Jamaal Williams added 67 yards and a touchdown on the ground. The Titans kept it interesting for a half behind Tyjae Spears's 110 rushing yards and two Caleb Ward touchdown passes, but Dallas pulled away in the second half.

The 21-point margin gives Bill a badly needed lift in the net points race, moving him back to plus-38 overall and keeping him in striking distance of the middle pack. He'll need both his teams to deliver in Week 12's gauntlet — the Cowboys host Matej's Eagles on Thanksgiving afternoon, then Bill's Steelers face Jordy's Broncos in a Friday afternoon head-to-head.

The week's first head-to-head went to Jordy as his Lions handled Adrian's Buccaneers 31-21 at Ford Field. Jared Goff was efficient with 279 yards and two touchdowns through the air, but it was Jahmyr Gibbs who stole the show on the ground — 98 yards and two scores on 23 carries, plus another 93 yards and a touchdown from Jameson Williams through the air. Tampa Bay stayed within striking distance behind Baker Mayfield's two touchdown passes, but could never get the stop they needed.

The head-to-head result is a double-edged sword for Jordy — yes, he pockets a full point while Adrian gets nothing, but Detroit's win also means his Lions can't make up any ground in the actual NFL standings where they're already a game ahead of the pack. Adrian's Bucs fall to 3-7 and are effectively eliminated from playoff contention, with his Patriots carrying whatever slim hope remains of salvaging something from this season.

Tymko's Chiefs looked like the Kansas City of old, dismantling Arizona 34-7 in a game that was never competitive. Patrick Mahomes carved up the Cardinals' secondary for 324 yards and three touchdowns on 27-of-39 passing, while Ervin Johnson pounded out 105 yards and a score on the ground. Travis Kelce caught six balls for 74 yards and two touchdowns, reminding everyone he's still got plenty left in the tank. Arizona managed just 155 passing yards and couldn't establish any run game.

The blowout moves Tymko to 14-6 and keeps him in third place, two games back of Chris and one clear of Ben. His Rams are on a bye this week, but the Chiefs face their stiffest test of the season Thursday night when they visit Chris's Bills in what could be the game of Thanksgiving — a head-to-head that will either pull Tymko within one game of the pool lead or push him three back.

Matej's Eagles squeaked past Bill's Steelers 19-16 in a defensive struggle in Philadelphia that came down to field position and field goals. Joe Milton managed just 141 yards through the air, but Saquon Barkley carried the load with 75 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries. Aaron Rodgers threw for 227 yards in the loss but could only find the end zone once, connecting with Miles Hurleman for a score. The Steelers moved the ball but couldn't finish drives.

The head-to-head victory pulls Matej even with Orest at 10 points, though Orest holds the net points tiebreaker by 54 points. Bill falls to 11-10 and now faces two massive head-to-heads in Week 12 — his Cowboys get Matej's Eagles again on Thanksgiving, then his Steelers host Jordy's Broncos on Friday afternoon. Bill needs to win at least one to stay relevant in the pool race.

The week's wildest finish came in Carolina, where Taras's Panthers held off Orest's Ravens 35-33 in a back-and-forth shootout. Bryce Young had his best game as a pro, going 22-of-30 for 254 yards and two touchdowns, while Chuba Hubbard bulldozed his way to 120 yards and two scores on 27 carries. Baltimore's Jacoby Brissett threw for 276 yards and Derrick Henry rumbled for 94 yards and a touchdown, but the Ravens couldn't get the stop they needed in the final minutes.

The head-to-head loss drops Orest to 10-11 and effectively ends any realistic shot at catching the leaders — his Ravens are now 4-7 in the actual standings and his Seahawks face Ben's red-hot Niners next Sunday. Taras picks up a crucial point to move to 6-14, still in last place but at least keeping Adrian within sight. His Chargers lost again to fall to 1-9, but at least his Panthers are 5-5 and hanging around the NFC wild card picture.

Taras's Chargers couldn't hold on at home, blowing a late lead to the Jets in a 27-24 defeat that drops Los Angeles to 1-9. Justin Herbert was efficient with 131 yards and two touchdowns on 15-of-21 passing, and Omarion Hampton rushed for 89 yards, but Geno Smith's three touchdown passes were too much. Breece Hall added 86 yards on the ground for New York in a game the Chargers desperately needed to win.

The loss is Taras's fifth straight with the Chargers and drops his net points to minus-113, by far the worst mark in the pool. His only hope now is that his Panthers can string together enough wins down the stretch to pull him out of the cellar — Carolina faces Adrian's Bucs on Monday Night Football in Week 12, a rare head-to-head opportunity for the pool's bottom two entrants.

Jordy's Broncos handled Las Vegas 38-24 at home behind a monster game from Jaleel Coleman, who rushed for 111 yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries. Bo Nix was solid if unspectacular with 225 yards and a touchdown through the air, while the defense did enough to contain Ashton Jeanty, who rushed for 79 yards and caught five balls for 90 yards and a score. The Raiders hung around into the fourth quarter but couldn't stop Denver's ground game.

The victory gives Jordy his second 2-0 week of the season and pushes him to 16-4, one game clear of Chris for the pool lead. His Broncos are 8-2 and firmly in the AFC playoff picture, while his Lions are 8-2 and running away with the NFC North. Jordy's gauntlet begins Friday afternoon when his Broncos visit Bill's Steelers in a head-to-head — if Denver wins, Jordy could stretch his lead to two or even three games depending on how Chris fares against Tymko on Thursday night.

Matej's Jaguars fell to the Giants 23-18 in a game Jacksonville desperately needed to keep pace in the AFC playoff race. Trevor Lawrence threw for 301 yards but was picked off twice and couldn't deliver in the clutch, while the Jags' run game managed just 33 yards on 10 carries from Braelon Tuten. J.J. McCarthy threw for just 173 yards for New York, but Malik Nabers caught seven balls for 55 yards and a touchdown, and the Giants' defense made enough plays to hold on.

The loss drops Matej's Jags to 7-3, still in decent playoff position but now tied atop the AFC South and needing to stay sharp down the stretch. Combined with his Eagles' win over Bill's Steelers, Matej finishes 1-1 for the week and stays at 10 points, tied for sixth place with Orest. He gets Tennessee at home next Sunday, a game Jacksonville should win, before facing a brutal December schedule.

Ben's Niners continued their dominance, throttling Minnesota 35-10 in a game that was never in doubt. Brock Purdy was surgical, going 21-of-26 for 255 yards and three touchdowns, while Christian McCaffrey added 49 yards and a score on the ground. Mike Evans caught six balls for 109 yards and a touchdown in one of San Francisco's most complete performances of the year. Kirk Cousins threw for 235 yards in the loss but was picked off once and couldn't get Minnesota into the end zone.

The blowout completes Ben's perfect 2-0 week and pushes him to 13-7, just one game back of Tymko for third place and within striking distance of Chris in second. His Niners are 9-1 and have clinched a playoff spot, while his Texans have clawed back to 4-6 and at least have a pulse. Ben faces two head-to-heads next weekend — Orest's Ravens visit Houston on Sunday afternoon, then Orest's Seahawks come to San Francisco later that day. If Ben sweeps, he'll be right in the thick of the pool race heading into December.

entrants.name: Ben
entrants.text: An absolute clinic — his Texans blanked the Colts 26-3 and his Niners dismantled Minnesota 35-10 for a 48-point net swing. He's now one game back of Tymko and within striking distance of second place. Week 12 brings two head-to-heads with Orest — Ravens at Texans on Sunday, then Seahawks at Niners later that afternoon.

entrants.name: Jordy
entrants.text: His Lions beat Adrian's Bucs 31-21 and his Broncos handled the Raiders 38-24 to push his pool lead to one full game over Chris. He's 16-4 and in complete control heading into a loaded Thanksgiving week. His Lions host Chicago on Thursday, then his Broncos visit Bill's Steelers on Friday afternoon in a head-to-head.

entrants.name: Chris
entrants.text: His Bills cruised past Miami 26-9 to stay 9-1 and atop the AFC, though the one-game week means he lost ground to Jordy. Week 12 brings two massive head-to-heads — his Pack face Tymko's Rams on Wednesday night, then his Bills host Tymko's Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

entrants.name: Tymko
entrants.text: His Chiefs demolished Arizona 34-7 in the week's most dominant performance, keeping him in third place at 14-6. His Rams were on a bye. Week 12 is make-or-break — he gets Chris twice, with the Rams hosting the Packers on Wednesday and the Chiefs visiting Buffalo on Thanksgiving night.

entrants.name: Bill
entrants.text: His Cowboys demolished Tennessee 51-30, but his Steelers fell to Matej's Eagles 19-16 in a head-to-head to leave him at 11-10 and in fifth place. Week 12 brings two more head-to-heads — his Cowboys host Matej's Eagles on Thanksgiving, then his Steelers get Jordy's Broncos on Friday.

entrants.name: Matej
entrants.text: His Eagles squeaked past Bill's Steelers 19-16 in a head-to-head, but his Jaguars fell to the Giants 23-18 to keep him at 10-10 and tied for sixth with Orest. He gets two more head-to-heads in Week 12 — Eagles at Bill's Cowboys on Thanksgiving, then Jags host Tennessee on Sunday.

entrants.name: Taras
entrants.text: His Panthers edged Orest's Ravens 35-33 in a head-to-head thriller, but his Chargers blew another late lead and lost to the Jets 27-24 to stay at 6-14 in last place. Week 12 brings two more head-to-heads — his Chargers host Adrian's Patriots on Sunday, then his Panthers visit Adrian's Bucs on Monday night.

entrants.name: Orest
entrants.text: His Ravens lost a 35-33 shootout to Taras's Panthers in a head-to-head that drops him to 10-11 and effectively ends any shot at the pool lead. His Seahawks were on a bye. Week 12 brings two head-to-heads with Ben — Ravens at Texans on Sunday, then Seahawks at Niners later that afternoon.

entrants.name: Adrian
entrants.text: His Bucs lost to Jordy's Lions 31-21 in a head-to-head to drop him to 8-12 and eighth place. His Patriots were on a bye. Week 12 brings two head-to-heads with Taras — Patriots at Chargers on Sunday, then Bucs host Panthers on Monday night. At 8-12, he needs to sweep to have any hope of climbing out of the bottom two.

ahead: Week 12 kicks off Wednesday night with Chris's Packers visiting Tymko's Rams in a critical head-to-head — winner stays within a game of Jordy, loser falls three back.
Thanksgiving brings three more pool collisions: Matej's Eagles at Bill's Cowboys in the afternoon, then Tymko's Chiefs at Chris's Bills on Thursday night — the latter could decide second place.

Friday afternoon features Jordy's Broncos at Bill's Steelers, then the weekend brings three more head-to-heads including Ben's double-dip with Orest and the Taras-Adrian basement battle on Monday night.
